newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas higher in Gulf, Mid-Con eases.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas higher in Gulf, Mid-Con eases.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices on the Gulf Coast pipes were slightly higher Friday despite cooler weather, while gas in the mid-continent was pushed lower by the mild temperatures, industry sources said.

Swing prices on the Gulf pipes rose one-three cents with some interest in storage buying and some market support from tension in the Middle East, the sources said. Prices were quoted in the low $1.80s per million British thermal units.
Despite the firmness in the Gulf, prices in the West and the Mid-Continent eased on milder temperatures and some cloud expected from the passing of Hurricane Fausto.
In the Midcontinent, prices edged lower to the mid-$1.60s with cool weather through much of the region.
Despite the moderate weather, sources said prices were finding some support at current levels.
"You might see people trying to catch up on storage with them able to buy at these cheap prices," one marketer said.
Prices at Waha were also weaker, falling in the afternoon to near $1.65 from talk at $1.68 in the morning, the sources said.
